allow_large: The owner chose on 2026-09-30 that sync writes subagent roles for both hosts; Forge's own eleven Codex role files are regenerated output of that sync, not hand-written code
done_when: forge sync writes Forge's eleven subagent roles for both hosts: .codex/agents/<role>.toml (name, description, developer_instructions, model, model_reasoning_effort) and .claude/agents/<role>.md (name, description, model, effort; no tools or permission mode, so roles inherit the session's). Each role takes its model and effort from forge.toml: worker, coder, frontend, tester and refactorer from build; explorer from lite; planner and architect from design (each host from its own family entry); debugger, security and performance from review. A kind whose model belongs to the other family leaves the model out on that host, so the role inherits the session model; Codex's ultra effort becomes max on Claude. Role instructions state today's Forge rules (no old constitution or write-scope wording). Sync refuses, changing nothing, when a client already has its own role file of the same name that Forge didn't write. Forge's own repo gets the same generated roles. Command-level tests check both hosts' files from a forge.toml, the family and effort mapping, the refusal, and that a second sync changes nothing.

findings.body: The Claude role writer inserts `model` and `effort` directly into YAML frontmatter. `src/forge/repo.py:261-265` accepts any string for these settings, so a valid TOML value containing an escaped newline, such as an effort followed by `tools: Bash`, produces an additional frontmatter field. This violates the requirement that roles inherit the session's tools and permission mode. Quote or validate these values as YAML scalars and cover the case through `forge sync`.
findings.title: Not done: keep tools and permission mode out of Claude roles

findings.body: For design roles, the host is already identified by `[models.design.claude]` or `[models.design.codex]`, but `_chosen` applies a name-based family guess afterward. `src/forge/repo.py:238-240` uses the family entry directly, and `tests/test_design_route.py` shows `custom-opus` is accepted and used for Claude work. With that valid setting, sync omits `model` from Claude's planner and architect roles because `custom-opus` does not start with a recognized prefix. Those roles then run on the session model instead of the configured design model.
findings.title: Not done: use each host's configured design model

findings.body: This change makes eleven named roles available to a coordinator in a client repo, but `src/forge/templates/skill.md` has no guidance for using them; its existing workflow still directs work only through Forge commands. The repository's review rule requires a change to what a coordinator or worker can use to update that template or the worker brief in the same change. The changed checked-in skill files add review-rule text, while the source template and brief remain unchanged.
findings.title: Not done: update the shipped Forge guidance for the new roles

findings.body: The command-level test checks only that instructions are nonempty, match between hosts, and omit three old phrases. It still passes if a role loses its test-first, commit, or no-push instructions and retains any unrelated sentence. The Done-when requirement that role instructions state today's Forge rules therefore lacks a test that fails when those rules disappear. Assert representative required instructions in the files produced by the real `forge sync` command.
findings.title: Not done: test that generated roles state current Forge rules

why: A Codex or Claude session opened directly in a client repo has none of Forge's subagent roles, so its subagents run on whatever model and effort the host picks instead of forge.toml's models
